title: EOL nginx 1.10.3 with known vulnerabilities (CVE-2017-7529)
description: nginx/1.10.3 (Ubuntu) is end-of-life and vulnerable to CVE-2017-7529 (integer overflow in range filter allowing info leak or DoS).
risks: Sensitive information disclosure from server memory; potential DoS; attacker reconnaissance advantage.
attack_vectors: Send crafted Range header requests to trigger CVE-2017-7529 buffer over-read. Exploit other nginx CVEs applicable to 1.10.x branch.
proof_of_existence: HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nServer: nginx/1.10.3 (Ubuntu)\n... confirmed in curl and whatweb output
remediation: Upgrade nginx to latest stable version (1.25+); remove Server header version disclosure

title: PrestaShop version not fingerprinted — CVE matching blocked
description: PrestaShop confirmed via Powered-By header and cookie naming. Exact version not determined, preventing CVE matching against known PrestaShop SQLi/RCE/XSS vulns.
risks: PrestaShop has multiple critical CVEs across versions (SQLi, RCE, path traversal, XSS). Unknown version means unknown exposure.
attack_vectors: Probe /admin/ panel, check JS/CSS asset paths for version hints, attempt known CVE exploits (e.g., CVE-2022-23648 path traversal, CVE-2023-30859).
proof_of_existence: Powered-By: PrestaShop\nSet-Cookie: PrestaShop-e1bd31adce7d8d5641fcc309e5c0c545=...\nrobots.txt: '# robots.txt automatically generated by PrestaShop'
remediation: Fingerprint exact PrestaShop version; upgrade to latest; remove Powered-By header

title: Outdated jQuery 1.7.1 with known XSS vulnerabilities
description: jQuery 1.7.1 is extremely outdated (released 2011). Vulnerable to CVE-2019-11358, CVE-2020-11022, CVE-2020-11023 (prototype pollution leading to XSS).
risks: XSS attacks via prototype pollution; potential account takeover; data exfiltration from client-side.
attack_vectors: Exploit jQuery prototype pollution to inject malicious properties into DOM objects, leading to XSS execution in user browsers.
proof_of_existence: whatweb output: JQuery[1.7.1] — confirmed version 1.7.1 in technology detection
remediation: Upgrade jQuery to latest 3.7.x; implement CSP headers to mitigate XSS

title: PHPSESSID cookie missing HttpOnly and Secure flags
description: PHPSESSID cookie set without HttpOnly or Secure attributes, enabling session theft via XSS or MITM attacks.
risks: Session hijacking via XSS-based cookie theft; session interception over non-encrypted connections.
attack_vectors: Combine with jQuery XSS to steal PHPSESSID via document.cookie; replay session to impersonate user.
proof_of_existence: Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=21n82sug41ght8rf1lof0ugdi2; path=/ — no HttpOnly, no Secure flags (contrast: PrestaShop cookie has both)
remediation: Set session.cookie_httponly=1 and session.cookie_secure=1 in php.ini

title: robots.txt discloses sensitive PrestaShop controller paths
description: robots.txt explicitly lists sensitive controller paths: authentication, cart, order, addresses, history, identity, my-account, order-detail, discount, get-file.
risks: Attackers can enumerate and target these endpoints for auth bypass, IDOR, or injection attacks.
attack_vectors: Probe listed controller paths for unauthenticated access, parameter tampering, or injection points. Target get-file controller for LFI.
remediation: Remove sensitive paths from robots.txt; rely on access controls instead of obscurity

title: Server version and technology stack disclosure
description: Server header reveals nginx/1.10.3 (Ubuntu); Powered-By header reveals PrestaShop; whatweb detected email contact@playtunisie.com.
risks: Attackers can target known vulnerabilities for exact software versions; email useful for phishing.
attack_vectors: Use disclosed versions to search CVE databases; craft targeted exploits for nginx 1.10.3 and PrestaShop.
remediation: Hide server version: server_tokens off; remove Powered-By header; obscure technology fingerprints

title: No sensitive files exposed (.env, .git, server-status)
description: Probes for .env, .git/HEAD, .git/config, and server-status all returned 404. Good security hygiene.
risks: No direct risk; positive finding confirming sensitive files are not publicly accessible.
attack_vectors: None confirmed; continue testing other paths like backup files, config.php, admin directories.
proof_of_existence: All returned HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found for .env, .git/HEAD, .git/config, server-status
remediation: No action needed; maintain current posture
